qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Transco right-of-way is physically irreplaceable, transporting ~15-20% of US natural gas with new greenfield interstate pipeline construction legally and politically unpermittable in the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast. However, the business fails the empirical capital efficiency proof: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is only 7.78% (peak 9.95% in 2023, 8.30% in 2025; 10-year range 1.84%–9.95%), well below the 12% hurdle. FERC cost-of-service and negotiated rate regulation structurally cap returns on invested capital while capital intensity remains perpetually high. Key erosion threats include FERC rate case challenges from utilities and long-term state-level building electrification/decarbonization mandates.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 7.78% vs 12% hurdle, REJECT). While the Transco pipeline network represents irreplaceable interstate energy infrastructure, high capital intensity and FERC utility rate regulation structurally constrain capital efficiency below the Munger hurdle across the entire 10-year cycle (GAAP ROIC never exceeded 10.0%, 10Y median 7.78%). Massive capital expenditures ($4.89B TTM in 2025) and heavy leverage ($27.3B debt vs $2.6B net income) permanently depress returns on total invested capital.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year historical GAAP ROIC averaged 5.4% and never reached the 12% threshold: 2016 (2.26%), 2017 (2.60%), 2018 (1.84%), 2019 (3.76%), 2020 (4.75%), 2021 (6.15%), 2022 (7.78%), 2023 (9.95%), 2024 (7.42%), and 2025 (8.30%). Tangible ROIC median is identically 7.78%. Segment revenue is anchored by Transmission & Gulf of Mexico (Transco, Northwest Pipeline) alongside Northeast and Western gathering & processing. While long-term reservation contracts provide volume stability, FERC cost-of-service rate base mechanisms limit economic rent extraction. Capital allocation is burdened by $27.32B in long-term debt against $63M cash, incurring $1.44B in annual interest expense against $4.20B EBIT (interest coverage 2.91x, below the 5.0x safe harbor threshold).
